name: kenspc
description: Structured software development workflows for Claude Code, aligned with Claude 5 generation guidance (last reviewed 2026-09-29): effort follows the session, with two overrides (high for unattended implementation and fixing). Skills cover project initialization (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and the project documents), brief generation, prototyping, plan generation, task decomposition, bug diagnosis, automated batch implementation, multi-angle parallel review whose final reports, like the autopilot's, carry a Merge danger section on what cannot be undone and how far a failure reaches, project guide generation, hand-started retrospectives over a window of finished batches that rank the problems recurring across batches, verify each proposed change against the raw records before the user sees it, and commit a record the next retro checks, and unattended batch runs to a release preparation, whose main session rules every point the spec leaves open and asks the user only on a stop condition and at its two gates, each role's worker at the model and effort the spec declares for it or at the main session's own, and its rails — no recursive rm, no write outside the repository, the workspace, and scratch — carried to every subagent it dispatches, in text and by a PreToolUse hook; thirteen reusable subagents do the review, fix, verification, implementation, and retro classification work. The v3 architecture follows six design rules: workflow SOP stays, business rules framed as why-not-command, DONE-criteria over step-by-step flow, no anti-rationalization scaffolding, plain language over MUST/NEVER/CRITICAL/ULTRATHINK, and review rubrics with named failure modes over generic checklists.
